The otsu column is a fixed global-intensity rule with two fitted parameters. Measured (results/noise_floors.json), its val-selected operating point is identical across every protocol (0.35) and its fitted cut varies only from 36.357 to 37.354, so its spread across test sets indexes test-set difficulty for a per-pixel rule. It is a sanity check, not a subtraction, and it is blind to CNN-specific differences (spec C5).

### Validation-to-test exchangeability by protocol

| Protocol | mean val IoU | mean test IoU | val minus test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| random overlapping patches | 0.2719 | 0.2861 | -0.0141 |
| random tiles | 0.2297 | 0.2329 | -0.0033 |
| random slices | 0.2824 | 0.2847 | -0.0023 |
| contiguous zones, no buffer | 0.3626 | 0.1931 | 0.1696 |
| zones + buffer 12 | 0.3540 | 0.2098 | 0.1442 |
| zones + buffer + straddler (reference) | 0.3695 | 0.2044 | 0.1651 |

Under a random split val and test are drawn from the same pool, so they agree and quoting either is equivalent. Under a contiguous split they are different regions of one meteorite and they do not. A paper using a contiguous split that reports validation performance overstates its held-out result by this column, before any training leakage is considered. This channel is independent of Finding 5: it is a gap measured WITHIN one protocol, so it does not depend on the between-protocol difference surviving replication.
